name: Romanticism
summary: Pictures of storm, sea, ruin, passion and distant lands, in which feeling comes before rule. Nature is vast and the person is small; colour and brush carry the mood.

philosophy.core_thesis: A picture should move the viewer by emotion and by awe, and so the painter puts feeling, nature and imagination above the cool rules of the academy.
design_principles: Make nature large and the figure small: a person at 5–15% of the picture height against a sky, a sea or a peak.
Open a deep space with a strong diagonal or a vortex, and lead the eye to a glowing horizon or a storm centre.
Use a dark, heavy foreground and a bright, burning distance: a value jump of 50% or more between them.
Choose a strong, warm and cold colour pair: a red or gold fire against a blue-green storm.
Show the hand: loose, wet strokes of 10–40mm in the sky and sea, and a hard edge only at the main figure.
Add a back-turned figure (Rückenfigur) or a wreck, so that the viewer stands inside the feeling.
Take the subject from history, literature, the exotic or the weather, and show the moment of peak action or loss.
anti_patterns: Cool, rational order with a calm, balanced layout
Smooth, hidden brushwork and a polished finish
A bright, even light with no drama
Figures that dominate and block the landscape

composition.layout: A deep space with a strong diagonal or a swirl, a dark mass in the foreground, and a burning or stormy light near the horizon at 35–45% of the height.
composition.focal_point: A small figure, a wreck or a flare of light, set at one third from an edge, where the diagonal and the brightest value meet.
composition.format: A wide or square canvas at 4:3 to 3:2; large for a history scene, small for a mood piece; the sky takes 40–60% of the height.

principles.rule: Set a figure at 5–15% of the picture height against a sky, a wave or a peak that fills 50% or more of the picture.
Make a jump of 50% or more in value between the dark foreground and the bright centre of light, and set warm against cold.
Lead the eye by one strong diagonal or a vortex at 30–50° from the horizontal to the point of light.
Place the one bright flare or small figure at the third line, and keep the rest of the picture under value 60%.
Build 3 to 4 layers of depth: a dark front, a middle ground, and a far, hazy light, with a strong loss of detail at each step.
Spend 60–70% of the area on a dark or stormy key, 20–30% on one glowing warm area, and 5–10% on a small accent.

palette.strategy: A dark, stormy key of brown, grey-blue and green, with one burning area of gold, orange or red; strong contrast of warm against cold.
palette.distribution: Dark and mid-tone mass 60–70%, glowing light area 20–30%, accent colour under 10%.
palette.ground: A warm brown or red-brown ground that shows through the dark areas.

brushwork_and_medium.medium: Oil paint with glazes and scumbles, and watercolour for rapid sketches of weather.
brushwork_and_medium.support: Canvas, often large, on a warm brown ground.
brushwork_and_medium.brushwork: Broad, wet strokes of 10–40mm in the sky and the sea, thicker dabs for the light, and fine strokes of 1–3mm at the figure.
brushwork_and_medium.paint_handling: Thin dark glazes in the shadow, thick impasto of 2–5mm in the highlights; wet-in-wet blending of the sky.
brushwork_and_medium.edges: Soft and lost edges in the sky, mist and sea; a hard edge at the main figure and the wreck.

light_and_modelling.light: A dramatic, low or burning source: a sunset, a storm gap, a fire or moonlight, set deep in the picture.
light_and_modelling.modelling: Strong, with 5–7 steps from dark to light; the form is shaped by the glow and loses detail in the dark.
light_and_modelling.shadow: Deep and large, 40–60% of the picture, with warm browns; the dark area is a mass with little detail.
light_and_modelling.temperature: A warm glow set against a cold storm; the warm area is small and the cold area is large.

subject.typical: Storm and wreck at sea, mountain and ruin, a lone wanderer, a lion hunt, a battle, a poem or a myth, and the east as an exotic scene.
subject.figure_scale: Small, at 5–15% of the picture height; in a history scene, large figures at 50–80%.
subject.treatment: Emotional, vast and personal; nature is a force and the person feels small and moved.

surface.finish: Semi-gloss with a rich varnish; the dark areas are deep.
surface.texture: Visible strokes in sky and sea, with thick, ridged light and smooth, thin shadow.

works.work: Fishing Boats with Hucksters Bargaining for Fish
Valley of Aosta: Snowstorm, Avalanche, and Thunderstorm

reference_works.note: Object ids were checked against the Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data). The Lion Hunt is a late work and the style at its most active. Look at the museum page for the image and its licence.

emotion.target_response: Awe and longing: the viewer feels small before a great force, and stirred by it.

use_cases: film poster for epic or sea stories
avoid_when: The brief needs a calm, technical or minimal mood.
The picture must show a small product in clear, even light.

modifiers.how: Drop the storm and the flare; use a flat grey day, plain figures at work, and a brown, earthy key with no glow.
Keep the sky and the water; raise the key to value 60% or more, break the stroke into dabs of 10–20mm, and remove the dark foreground.

sources.title: Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 data)
